_about: Resource budget for the Pip product firmware (--features physical-st7789, release). Checked without hardware by `just fw-budget` (scripts/firmware-budget.mjs) and in the firmware CI job. Set on 2026-10-31 from the build after PR #150 and cross-checked against the unit: device-measured peak stack use 115,740 B vs the 115,744 B this check derives. To change a limit on purpose, edit it here with the reason; see docs/virtual-pip.md (Hardware parity).

app_image_bytes.why: Loadable sections (text, rodata, data) were 343,686 B. About 5% headroom; the app partition is far larger, so this is a regression tripwire, not the physical limit.

asset_blob_bytes.why: The compiled asset blob was 127,253 B. The hard cap (ASSET_BLOB_CAP_BYTES, 131,072 B) is read from firmware/pip/src/internals.rs and checked too; this is a tighter early warning.

static_ram_bytes.why: Static RAM (data + bss) was 158,332 B. Everything above it comes out of the stack region, which is the rest of data RAM.

stack_region_bytes.why: The stack region (_stack_start - _stack_end) was 162,180 B. It must not shrink: the peak below leaves about 46 KiB free on the unit.

default_frame_bytes.why: Any function with a bigger frame must be listed in large_frames with its own ceiling, so a new large frame is a decision, not an accident.

worst_stack_bytes.why: Direct call chain from the entry was 115,744 B (boot, load_assets with the inlined AssetBlob::parse and the postcard Vec<SceneDef,8> visitor). The unit measured 115,740 B. About 4% headroom for the regression gate.

indirect_allowance_bytes.why: Calls through a register (trait objects, fn pointers) cannot be followed. The deepest chain under any function that no direct call reaches (not the entry or the trap vectors) was 384 B; this allows a hop of that kind with a 2.5x margin. Re-derive if an indirect callee grows a big frame.

interrupt_margin_bytes.why: Added on top of the traced interrupt path (interrupt_path) for the parts of an interrupt that are not followed.

stack_margin_bytes.why: The estimated peak plus the allowances plus this margin must fit the stack region. 16 KiB is slack for what the static estimate cannot see (compiler changes between toolchain versions).

large_frames.why: Boot only: the inlined AssetBlob::parse holds the manifest (Vec<SceneDef,8> and the bitmap table). It sets the stack peak.
Boot only: postcard builds the Vec<SceneDef,8> by value, below load_assets.
The run loop's locals; lives for the whole session.
Owns the peripherals and the display buffers' setup; lives for the whole session.
Input handling with the inlined scene transitions.
Frame decode and dispatch with the inlined handlers.
Boot only: postcard builds the bitmap table.
Frame encode with the inlined senders.

int64_division_allowlist.why: Once at boot: clock setup in esp-hal.
esp-hal's blocking delay (panel init); not in the frame path.
Rotary interrupt: scales the edge timestamp. Known debt; keep it cheap.
The run loop's clock and window arithmetic (once per tick, not per pixel).
Animation time scaling, once per frame. Known debt.
Gaze interpolation, once per frame. Known debt.
Line setup (slope), per line not per pixel. Known debt.
Per-sprite setup (4 call sites), not per pixel. Known debt; before PR #150 the same class of call in the pixel path made frames 4x slower.

The scene loop length (`frame_count * 1000 * fps.den / fps.num`, compositor.rs), once per frame, not per pixel. Unchanged source: the BuildInfo message (build id) changed which function LTO inlines it into, so it now shows here. The frame-cost fixture is unchanged and passes.
